correctness.rationale: Encode every two-chain linear extension as a monotone gap vector and queries as rectangular-grid ideal membership. The standard antichain argument gives VC=min(a,b). Independent direct enumeration of all 35 (3,4) interleavings gave the smaller root-branch counts rows (15,10,4,1),(5,13,13,5),(1,4,10,15): each root has at most 15 concepts in one branch, preventing depth five (requires 16 each). A separate memoized Littlestone recursion over exact membership-mask splits computed all twelve unordered positive two-chain profiles through total size seven: (3,4) has Ldim=4, entropy bound=5; every other profile saturates the bound. This validates the witness lower bound and minimality without relying on saved verification_output.txt. No claim is made for all chain sizes.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive verification is restricted to its specified domain.

value.rationale: This identifies a sharp and mathematically motivated first entropy-cardinality obstruction for adaptive shattering of linear extensions, with explicit difference from the static grid width. It gives a canonical small counterexample to assuming that concept-count information always controls online comparison depth. An exact first obstruction is useful without an all-parameter recurrence.
residual_risks: The value is finite or parameter-specific and should not be promoted as an all-parameter theorem.

final_claim: Two-chain interleaving comparison classes have VC dimension min(a,b); Littlestone meets floor(log2 binomial(a+b,a)) for totals <=6, and the only total-seven obstruction is (3,4), with Ldim=4<5 and VC=3.
limitations: Only the first obstruction through total chain length seven; no unrestricted recurrence or query-optimal merge sorting theorem.
